stem: On a q-sphere, a node (marker) is drawn at every computational basis state whose amplitude is nonzero. For the state below, which basis states appear as nodes? (Select 2.)
code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
from qiskit.visualization import plot_state_qsphere

qc = QuantumCircuit(3)
qc.h(1)
qc.x(2)
state = Statevector.from_instruction(qc)
fig = plot_state_qsphere(state)

explanation.correct: H puts qubit 1 into a superposition and X sets qubit 2 to |1>; qubit 0 is untouched. In Qiskit's little-endian labels the string reads q2 q1 q0, so the state is (|100> + |110>)/√2 — qubit 2 is the leftmost character and is always 1, qubit 1 is the middle character and takes both values, qubit 0 is the rightmost and stays 0. Only those two basis states carry amplitude, so the q-sphere shows two nodes; node size encodes each amplitude's magnitude and node color its phase.

distractors.A: |000> would need qubit 2 to be |0>, but the X gate flipped it to |1>. Forgetting the X leaves you with the two nodes of a bare Hadamard.
distractors.B: |001> is the label of |100> read backwards, as if the leftmost character were qubit 0. Qiskit prints the highest-index qubit on the LEFT, so the X on qubit 2 shows up leftmost.
distractors.C: |011> is |110> read backwards — the same big-endian habit as the other reversed label. Under Qiskit's convention the set bits stay at the positions of qubits 2 and 1, which are the two leftmost characters.
distractors.E: |101> would require qubit 0 to be |1>, but nothing acts on qubit 0. This is the pair of nodes you get if the Hadamard is misread as acting on qubit 0 rather than qubit 1.

provenance.notes: official-alignment fix wave 2026-07-26: widened from 2 to 3 qubits so the option set can hold a distractor pool. The 2-qubit version listed ALL four basis states, so no fifth option could be a basis state (REVIEW_LEDGER: 'whole-basis questions cannot be pooled'); on 3 qubits six of the eight basis states are offered, every option stays a legal basis state, and display_count 5 rotates 3 of the 4 distractors.
